topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the lecture's learning objectives regarding cancer etiology.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Chance, Genetics, and Environmental Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the fundamental causes of cancer, contrasting intrinsic replicative errors and genetic predisposition with environmental exposures using population data and epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenic Agents, Mutagens, and Promoters
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how specific infectious, chemical, and physical agents induce malignancy through biological mechanisms such as metabolic activation, direct DNA damage, chronic inflammation, and tumor promotion.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogen exposure signatures and test whether specific agents induce cancer.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Closing Remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of the environmental impact on cancer, the challenges of determining carcinogenicity, and everyday risk-benefit decisions.
